source.name: NASA Mars 2020 raw images
source.readFrom: local working copy, first read from NASA's raw image feed

how: Up to 6 full frames from the left navigation camera for each rover stop in the box, spread around the mast's turn, looking between -35 and 10 degrees from the horizon, and only above -20 degrees where a stop has at least 3 such frames. A photo is placed at a stop only when the feed's own site and drive numbers match that stop.
caveats: A photo shows the view from where the rover stood, about 2 m above the ground, on the day it was taken.
Which way a photo faces on the map is not given: the mast's azimuth is stored as the feed gives it and we have not confirmed what it is measured from.
